params.claimNft: If `false`, NFTs are NOT dispensed and the NFT cursor                  is NOT advanced. The caller still loses the chance to                  claim later (`claimed` flag is set). Useful for users                  who only want their ZKP and want to skip the gas of                  receiving NFTs.
params.nftCount: Number of PNFTs the caller is entitled to (committed                  in the Merkle leaf). Must match the leaf even if                  `claimNft == false`.
params.proof: Merkle proof for leaf                  `keccak256(bytes.concat(keccak256(abi.encode(                      msg.sender, zkpAmount, nftCount                  ))))`.
params.zkpAmount: Amount of ZKP to receive (in wei).

CLAIM_WINDOW().notice: Time after `setRoot` during which only users can withdraw via `claim`. The owner sweep functions revert until this window has passed.

FIRST_NFT_ID().notice: First PNFT tokenId held by this Vault (inclusive). Verified on-chain: PNftToken's internal counter starts at 1, and `ownerOf(0)` reverts ("invalid token ID") at the time of deployment.

LAST_NFT_ID().notice: Last PNFT tokenId held by this Vault (inclusive). Verified on-chain: `NFT.balanceOf(vault) == 2000`, `ownerOf(2000) == vault`, and `ownerOf(2001)` reverts at the time of deployment.

NFT_TOKEN().notice: The ERC-721 token (PNFT) that funded the advanced-stake rewards.

OWNER().notice: The owner who has privileged rights

ZKP_TOKEN().notice: The ERC-20 token (PZKP) that funded the advanced-stake rewards.

claimOpenedAt().notice: Block timestamp at which `setRoot` was called. The owner sweep functions unlock at `claimOpenedAt + CLAIM_WINDOW`. Zero until `setRoot` is called.

claimed(address).notice: Per-address claim flag. A user can claim at most once.

isClaimOpen().notice: Whether claims are open (i.e. the Merkle root has been set).

isClaimable(address,uint256,uint16,bool,.notice: Combined predicate the UI can hit in a single eth_call: would `claim(zkpAmount, nftCount, claimNft, proof)` from `user` currently succeed?

nextNftId().notice: The PNFT tokenId that the next claim would start at. The next claim of `n` NFTs receives ids `[nextNftId, nextNftId + n - 1]`.

nftsClaimed().notice: Total PNFTs dispensed so far. The next claim starts at `FIRST_NFT_ID + nftsClaimed`.

nftsRemaining().notice: Number of PNFTs still held by this Vault and not yet dispensed.

ownerSweepErc20(address,address,uint256).notice: Sweep an ERC-20 balance to `to`. Intended for residual ZKP that stays unclaimed after the 1-year claim window ends.

ownerSweepNft(address,uint256[]).notice: Sweep a list of PNFT tokenIds to `to`. Used to recover NFTs that no one claimed after the 1-year claim window ends.

root().notice: Merkle root committing the (user, zkpAmount, nftCount) tuples. Settable exactly once by `OWNER`, in a follow-up proposal after this implementation is in place and the entitlement set is finalised.

setRoot(bytes32).notice: Commit the entitlement Merkle root. May only be called once. Records the timestamp so the owner sweep functions unlock exactly `CLAIM_WINDOW` later.

sweepUnlocksAt().notice: Unix timestamp at which the owner sweep functions unlock. Returns 0 if `setRoot` has not yet been called.

verifyClaim(address,uint256,uint16,bytes.notice: Verify the Merkle proof for the (`user`, `zkpAmount`, `nftCount`) tuple against the current root. Does NOT check the `claimed` flag.

userdoc.notice: Frozen replacement implementation for the v0 Vault behind the existing Vault proxy on Polygon. Effects of upgrading the Vault proxy to this implementation:   - `lockAsset` and `unlockAsset` always revert, regardless of caller.     `PantherPoolV0.exit()` and `PantherPoolV0.generateDeposits()` therefore     revert too — the v0 MASP path is permanently disabled.   - Rewards previously locked here (ZKP and PNFT) become claimable through     a Merkle-tree-based `claim` function, with eligibility computed off-chain     from the on-chain stake / reward / exit history and committed via a     single Merkle `root` set once by the new owner. Storage layout: the prior implementation had no storage of its own (only immutables in `ImmutableOwnable`). Variables added here therefore start at slot 0 with no collision risk. Do not reorder, remove, or insert into the storage variable list below without a coordinated migration.
